description: An in-depth study of relational database design, keys, relationships, integrity, normalisation and writing basic SQL statements to create and manipulate data.

mcq.questionText: In a relational database, what is the correct term for a single horizontal entry that holds all the data about one item, such as one student?
mcq.explanation: A record, also called a row or tuple, is one complete set of related data about a single item. A field (column) holds only one attribute of that item.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes the difference between data and information?

options.text: Data is always stored on paper while information is stored on computers
Data is raw, unprocessed facts while information is processed data that has meaning
Data is numbers while information is words
Data and information mean exactly the same thing

mcq.explanation: Data refers to raw facts and figures with no context, while information is the result of processing and organising that data so it becomes meaningful and useful.

mcq.questionText: What is the role of a DBMS such as Microsoft Access, MySQL or Oracle?

options.text: It is the collection of related data itself
It is software used to create, store, manage and retrieve data in a database
It is a single table inside a database
It is a printed report produced from a database

mcq.explanation: A database is the organised collection of data, while a DBMS (Database Management System) is the software that lets users create and manage that database.

mcq.questionText: A column in a database table is uniquely identified by which property of an entity?
mcq.explanation: Each column represents an attribute (field) of the entity, for example StudentName or DateOfBirth. Each record then supplies a value for every attribute.

mcq.questionText: Which key is a field in one table that refers to the primary key of another table to link the two tables together?
mcq.explanation: A foreign key is a field that holds values matching the primary key of another table, creating a relationship and enforcing referential integrity between the tables.

mcq.questionText: A primary key made up of two or more fields combined to uniquely identify a record is called a:
mcq.explanation: A composite (compound) key uses a combination of two or more columns to uniquely identify each record when no single column is unique on its own.

mcq.questionText: In which relationship can ONE record in Table A be linked to MANY records in Table B, but each record in Table B links back to only one record in Table A?
mcq.explanation: A one-to-many relationship, for example one class having many students, is the most common relationship type in relational databases.

mcq.questionText:
Consider this table named Students:

ID | Name   | Class | Marks
1  | Asha   | F4A   | 78
2  | Juma   | F4B   | 55
3  | Neema  | F4A   | 91

Which SQL statement returns ONLY the names of students whose Marks are greater than 60?

options.text: SELECT Name FROM Students WHERE Marks > 60;
SELECT Marks FROM Students WHERE Name > 60;
GET Name FROM Students IF Marks > 60;
SELECT ALL FROM Students WHERE Marks = 60;

mcq.explanation: SELECT Name picks the column to display, FROM Students names the table, and WHERE Marks > 60 filters the rows, returning Asha and Neema.

mcq.questionText: Which SQL clause is used to arrange the results of a query in a particular sequence, such as alphabetical or numerical order?
mcq.explanation: ORDER BY sorts the result set; adding ASC sorts ascending (the default) and DESC sorts descending.

mcq.questionText: Which SQL statement correctly adds a new record into a table called Teachers with columns ID and Name?

options.text: INSERT Teachers VALUES ID = 5 AND Name = 'Mussa';

mcq.explanation: The INSERT INTO statement uses the form INSERT INTO table (columns) VALUES (values); text values are placed inside single quotes.

mcq.questionText:
What does the following SQL statement do?

DELETE FROM Students WHERE Class = 'F4B';

options.text: It deletes the whole Students table from the database
It deletes only the records where the Class is F4B
It deletes the Class column from the table
It changes every Class value to F4B

mcq.explanation: DELETE FROM removes rows; the WHERE clause restricts deletion to only those records matching Class = 'F4B'. Without WHERE, all rows would be removed.

mcq.questionText: Which SQL statement correctly creates a simple table named Books with a text column Title and a number column Year?

options.text: CREATE TABLE Books (Title TEXT, Year INTEGER);
CREATE Books TABLE WITH Title, Year;
NEW TABLE Books (Title TEXT, Year INTEGER);

mcq.explanation: CREATE TABLE is followed by the table name and a list of columns with their data types inside parentheses, such as TEXT and INTEGER.

mcq.questionText: Organising data to reduce repetition and avoid storing the same information many times is known as:
mcq.explanation: Normalisation is the process of splitting data into related tables to remove redundancy and reduce update problems, keeping the database efficient and consistent.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of using a database instead of separate flat files?

options.text: It always uses less electricity than paper records
It reduces data redundancy and allows data to be shared and updated consistently
It removes the need for any data security
It makes searching for records slower and harder

mcq.explanation: Databases reduce duplication, keep data consistent, allow controlled sharing and provide faster, more reliable searching than separate flat files.

mcq.questionText: A school wants students and the many clubs they join to be linked, where one student can join many clubs and one club can have many students. How is this many-to-many relationship usually implemented in a relational database?

options.text: By placing all data in one single large table
By creating a third (junction) table that links the two tables using their primary keys
By using a one-to-one relationship instead
By deleting the foreign keys from both tables

mcq.explanation: A many-to-many relationship is resolved by introducing a junction (link) table that holds foreign keys referring to the primary keys of both original tables.

fib.questionText: Raw, unprocessed facts and figures that have not yet been given meaning are called _____.
fib.explanation: Data is the raw input; once processed and organised it becomes information.

fib.questionText: The software used to create and manage a database is known by the abbreviation _____.
fib.explanation: DBMS stands for Database Management System, for example Microsoft Access, MySQL or Oracle.

fib.questionText: A field that uniquely identifies each record in a table is called the _____ key.
fib.explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies every record and cannot contain duplicate or null values.

fib.questionText: A field in one table that links to the primary key of another table is called a _____ key.
fib.explanation: A foreign key creates relationships between tables and enforces referential integrity.

fib.questionText: In SQL, the clause used to filter records based on a given condition is the _____ clause.
fib.explanation: The WHERE clause selects only the rows that satisfy the stated condition.

fib.questionText: To change the value of existing records in a table, the SQL command _____ is used together with SET.
fib.explanation: UPDATE table SET column = value WHERE condition modifies existing records.

fib.questionText: Complete the SQL: SELECT * FROM Students _____ Class = 'F4A'; to show only Form 4A students.
fib.explanation: WHERE Class = 'F4A' filters the rows so that only Form 4A records are returned.

fib.questionText: The process of organising data into tables to remove duplication and redundancy is called _____.
fib.explanation: Normalisation reduces redundancy and avoids update, insertion and deletion problems.

fib.questionText: A database object that presents data in a printable, well-formatted layout for output is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A report formats data, often from queries or tables, for printing or presentation.

fib.questionText: Keeping a duplicate copy of a database in a safe place so it can be restored after loss is called taking a _____.
fib.explanation: A backup is a copy of data kept so the database can be recovered if the original is damaged or lost.

tf.questionText: A database and a DBMS are exactly the same thing.
tf.explanation: A database is the organised collection of data, while a DBMS is the software used to create and manage that database.

tf.questionText: In a relational database table, a column represents a field (attribute) and a row represents a record.
tf.explanation: Columns are the fields or attributes, and each row is one complete record about an item.

tf.questionText: A primary key is allowed to contain duplicate values in different records.
tf.explanation: A primary key must be unique for every record and cannot contain duplicate or null values.

tf.questionText: A foreign key is used to create a relationship between two tables.
tf.explanation: A foreign key in one table matches the primary key of another table, linking the two together.

tf.questionText: The SQL statement DELETE FROM Students; without a WHERE clause removes all records from the Students table.
tf.explanation: Without a WHERE clause DELETE FROM removes every row in the table, so it must be used carefully.

tf.questionText: The ORDER BY clause in SQL is used to filter records, not to sort them.
tf.explanation: ORDER BY sorts the result set; it is the WHERE clause that filters records.

tf.questionText: Normalisation is intended to increase the amount of duplicate data stored in a database.
tf.explanation: Normalisation reduces, not increases, duplication and redundancy by organising data into related tables.

tf.questionText: A many-to-many relationship is usually implemented using a junction (link) table.
tf.explanation: A junction table with foreign keys to both tables resolves a many-to-many relationship into two one-to-many relationships.

tf.questionText: Data integrity means ensuring that the data stored in a database is accurate, valid and consistent.
tf.explanation: Data integrity rules keep stored data correct, complete and consistent across the database.

tf.questionText: Using passwords and access rights to control who can view or change data is a method of database security.
tf.explanation: Passwords, user accounts and access rights restrict access and help protect data from unauthorised use.

summary.questionText: Define the term database in one sentence.
summary.correctAnswer: A database is an organised collection of related data stored together so that it can be easily accessed, managed and updated.
summary.explanation: The key idea is organised, related data stored for easy access and management.

summary.questionText: State the difference between a primary key and a foreign key.
summary.correctAnswer: A primary key uniquely identifies each record in its own table, while a foreign key is a field that refers to the primary key of another table to link the tables.
summary.explanation: Primary key = unique identifier in its table; foreign key = link to another table's primary key.

summary.questionText: List the three main types of relationships between tables in a relational database.
summary.explanation: These three relationship types describe how records in one table relate to records in another.

summary.questionText: Name four common database objects found in a DBMS such as Microsoft Access.
summary.explanation: Tables store data, queries retrieve and filter data, forms aid data entry, and reports present data for output.

summary.questionText: Explain the purpose of the WHERE clause in an SQL statement.
summary.correctAnswer: The WHERE clause selects only the records that meet a stated condition, filtering the rows acted upon or returned.
summary.explanation: WHERE limits SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE to records matching the condition.

summary.questionText: Write an SQL statement that selects all columns from a table called Employees where the Department is 'Sales'.
summary.explanation: SELECT * returns all columns, FROM names the table, and WHERE filters to the Sales department.

summary.questionText: State two advantages of using a database over separate flat files.
summary.correctAnswer: It reduces data redundancy (duplication) and keeps data consistent, and it allows data to be shared and searched quickly and securely.
summary.explanation: Reduced redundancy, consistency, controlled sharing and faster searching are key database advantages.

summary.questionText: What is normalisation and why is it important?
summary.correctAnswer: Normalisation is the process of organising data into related tables to remove redundancy; it is important because it saves storage, prevents inconsistent data and avoids update problems.
summary.explanation: Normalisation reduces duplication and keeps the database efficient and consistent.

summary.questionText: Write an SQL statement that changes the Marks to 80 for the student with ID 3 in a table called Students.
summary.correctAnswer: UPDATE Students SET Marks = 80 WHERE ID = 3;
summary.explanation: UPDATE with SET changes the column value, and WHERE ID = 3 limits the change to that one record.

summary.questionText: Give two methods used to keep data in a database secure.
summary.correctAnswer: Using passwords and user access rights to control access, and taking regular backups to protect against data loss.
summary.explanation: Access control (passwords, rights) and backups are core data security and protection measures.

hoq.questionText: A library stores each Member and the many Books each member borrows over time, where one member borrows many books but each borrowing record relates to one member. A designer puts the member's full name and phone number inside every borrowing record instead of in a separate Members table. Which problem is MOST directly caused by this design?

options.text: The database cannot use SQL at all
Data redundancy, because the same member details are repeated and may become inconsistent
The primary key automatically becomes a foreign key
Reports can no longer be printed from the database

hoq.explanation: Repeating member details in every borrowing record causes redundancy and update anomalies; normalisation fixes this by storing member details once in a Members table linked by a foreign key.

hoq.questionText:
Given this table named Stock:

ItemID | Item    | Quantity
1      | Pens    | 5
2      | Books   | 40
3      | Rulers  | 12
4      | Bags    | 3

A shopkeeper runs:
SELECT Item FROM Stock WHERE Quantity < 10 ORDER BY Quantity DESC;
Which result is produced?
hoq.explanation: WHERE Quantity < 10 keeps Pens (5) and Bags (3). ORDER BY Quantity DESC sorts highest first, so Pens (5) comes before Bags (3), giving Pens, Bags.

hoq.questionText: A clerk wants to remove every product in a Products table whose Price is 0, but accidentally writes: DELETE FROM Products; and runs it. What is the consequence, and what was the correct statement?

options.text: Only products with Price 0 are deleted; the statement was already correct
Nothing happens because DELETE always needs WHERE to run
All records in Products are deleted; the correct statement was DELETE FROM Products WHERE Price = 0;
The Price column is removed but the records remain; correct statement was DROP Price;

hoq.explanation: DELETE FROM Products; has no WHERE clause, so it removes every record. The intended statement needed a WHERE clause: DELETE FROM Products WHERE Price = 0;
